item.title: Inside the Rushed Effort to Get Trump His New Air Force One
item.description: A New York Times investigation found that President Trump’s push to speed delivery of the aircraft led to ballooning costs and trade-offs in safety features.
item.dc:creator: Eric Lipton, Tyler Pager and Maggie Haberman
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: President Trump walked off the new Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews on July 9 after attending a NATO summit in Turkey. A security threat was said to have altered his trip.

item.title: President Trump’s New Air Force One Poses Potential Security Risks
item.description: Our investigative reporter Eric Lipton explains how earlier this month President Trump abruptly switched aircraft when leaving Turkey because of a credible threat that Iranian proxies were targeting a new Air Force One that had omitted key security modifications needed for a Qatari Boeing 747.
item.dc:creator: Eric Lipton, Nour Idriss, Nikolay Nikolov, Thomas Vollkommer, Stephanie Swart, Rafaela Balster, Arfa Momin, Junho Lee, Whitney Shefte and Paul Abowd

item.title: How a Housing Bill Trump Spurned Became Law
item.description: Despite partisan differences, intraparty feuds and the president’s lack of interest, Congress delivered the first major housing bill in a generation.
item.dc:creator: Ronda Kaysen
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: The high cost of housing has been a burden in Democratic cities for years but since the pandemic, conservative states like Idaho and Montana also experienced increases in rents and home prices.

item.title: After Democratic Shake-Up, Susan Collins Holds Enormous Cash Edge in Maine
item.description: Republicans are pouring huge sums behind the Maine senator through a web of billionaire-funded super PACs. Troy Jackson, the likely Democratic nominee, has a lot of catching up to do.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner, Lisa Lerer and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Ryan David Brown for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Susan Collins’s campaign and its Republican allies have reserved about $60 million in airtime through the fall.
